summary: Neal Donner specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Leon Hurvitz at the University of British Columbia (attested 1976).
Neelima Mundayar works in religious studies and Indology. She pursued her PhD at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Wilfried Swenden (attested 2026).

Nenghai Shi (1886–1967) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Peking University under Kecheng Zhang, trained with several traditional teachers, founded the Shaocheng Society of Buddhist Studies (1917), and served as vice-president of the Buddhist Association of China (1953–1966).
Newton Mohun Dutt worked in Indology and served as Curator of Libraries for Baroda State and at the Central Library of Vadodara from circa 1913 to 1934.
Ng-Fung Yuen works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Yuen completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under the supervision of Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngakchang Gönpo Tsé Ten studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ngan-che Chan works in Buddhist studies. Chan completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin (attested 2007) and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.
Ngawang Jorden works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held posts at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
Ngawang Lek Shé Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Ngawang Nyima worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche, and taught Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, and taught numerous students, including Ngulchu Yangchen Drubpai Dorje.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at Punjabi University under supervisor Inder Mohan Singh (attested 2012) and also studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet (attested 2012).
Nguyen Thi Xinh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed a PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi, where he completed an MA under the supervision of Karam Tej Singh Sarao.
Nhu Lien specializes in Buddhist studies, having studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under the teacher Ādiccavaṃsa.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under teachers including Lianju Xia. He worked as head of the Central People's Broadcasting Station and as a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was active in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Rissho, Taisho, and Koyasan Universities, as well as Horyuji Kangakuin and Kennin-ji, and founded Nipponzan-Myohoji.

Nicholas Dirks (born 1950) is a historian and Indologist who studied at Wesleyan University (~1968–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981). He held posts at Caltech (~1978–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).
